subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: If the forward reaction of a reversible reaction is endothermic, what is the reverse reaction?
questions.explain: If the forward direction is endothermic, the reverse direction releases the same energy, so it is exothermic.

questions.q: On a reaction profile for an endothermic reaction, the products line is drawn:
questions.explain: Endothermic products store more energy, so the products line is higher than the reactants.

questions.q: Adding a catalyst changes a reaction profile by:
options: Raising the energy of the products
Lowering the energy of the reactants
questions.explain: A catalyst provides a route with a lower activation energy, shown as a smaller hump on the profile.

questions.q: On a reaction profile, the activation energy is:
options: The energy of the products only
The minimum energy needed to start the reaction
The energy difference between reactants and products
questions.explain: Activation energy is the minimum energy needed for reactant particles to react, shown as the hump on the profile.

questions.q: A reaction is exothermic overall when:
options: More energy is released making bonds than absorbed breaking bonds
More energy is absorbed breaking bonds than released making bonds
Equal energy is absorbed and released
questions.explain: If bond-making releases more energy than bond-breaking absorbs, the reaction is exothermic overall.

questions.q: Is bond making endothermic or exothermic?
questions.explain: Forming new bonds releases energy, so it is exothermic.

questions.q: In a chemical cell, the voltage produced depends on:
options: The difference in reactivity of the two electrode metals
The temperature of the room only
questions.explain: A bigger difference in reactivity between the two metal electrodes produces a larger voltage.

questions.q: In a hydrogen fuel cell, hydrogen and oxygen combine to produce:
questions.explain: A hydrogen fuel cell produces only water (and electrical energy) as hydrogen reacts with oxygen.

questions.q: Which of these is an endothermic process?
questions.explain: Thermal decomposition takes in energy from the surroundings, so it is endothermic.

questions.q: Which process is endothermic and is used in instant cold packs?
options: Dissolving certain salts such as ammonium nitrate
questions.explain: Dissolving ammonium nitrate takes in energy from the surroundings, cooling the pack.

questions.q: When citric acid reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate, the temperature falls. This reaction is:
questions.explain: The temperature drop shows energy is taken in, so the reaction is endothermic.

questions.q: Lowering the temperature of a reaction decreases the rate because particles:
options: Collide less often and with less energy
questions.explain: Cooler particles move more slowly, so they collide less frequently and with less energy.

questions.q: Using bond energies, a reaction is endothermic if:
options: More energy is needed to break bonds than is released making them
Less energy is needed to break bonds than is released making them
questions.explain: If breaking bonds needs more energy than is released making bonds, the reaction takes in energy overall.

questions.q: Why does a catalyst not change the amount of product made?
options: It is used up in the reaction
It only changes how fast equilibrium or completion is reached
questions.explain: A catalyst only speeds up the rate; it does not change the quantity of product formed.

questions.q: Why does a non-rechargeable battery eventually stop working?
options: One of the reactants is used up
questions.explain: In a non-rechargeable cell the reaction stops once one of the reactants is used up.

questions.q: What is a key disadvantage of hydrogen fuel cells?
options: Hydrogen is difficult and costly to store and transport
questions.explain: Storing and transporting hydrogen safely is difficult and expensive, a key drawback of fuel cells.

questions.q: Increasing the pressure of reacting gases increases the rate because:
options: The particles are closer together so collide more frequently
questions.explain: Higher pressure squeezes gas particles closer, increasing collision frequency.

questions.q: On the reaction profile of an exothermic reaction, the products are:
options: At the same energy as the reactants
Lower in energy than the reactants
Higher in energy than the reactants
questions.explain: In an exothermic reaction the products have less energy than the reactants, so the line ends lower.

questions.q: According to collision theory, for a reaction to occur particles must collide and have at least what?
questions.explain: Particles must collide with energy equal to or greater than the activation energy to react.

questions.q: In a simple chemical cell, a greater voltage is produced when the two metals are:
options: Further apart in the reactivity series
questions.explain: The bigger the difference in reactivity between the two metals, the larger the voltage produced.

questions.q: An advantage of a hydrogen fuel cell over a petrol engine is that it:
options: Stores more energy than any battery
Produces only water as a product
questions.explain: Fuel cells produce only water, so they release no carbon dioxide at the point of use.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an exothermic process?
options: Neutralisation of an acid and alkali
questions.explain: Neutralisation releases energy, so the temperature of the mixture rises — it is exothermic.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) Chemistry (1CH0) specification; Rates Of Reaction Energy Changes
